title: Picking versus bowing among the early bassists
summary: Breaux says most players picked rather than bowed in his day and names those who bowed well.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: In those days, did they pick most of the time or did some of them use the bow? How did they do when you were a kid?

Well, when I came along, it was just about breaking ice with the bow. I mean, everybody was going to pick. And it was very little bowing I've seen. Chester did a nice job on bowing. And Mr. Glennon did. And old man Mitchell, Harmon Mitchell's daddy, he'd bow pretty well. But the majority of the fellas, Cleo and myself, we never bothered with the bow. I did a very, very little bowing.
Well, you knew the fellas during the time of Glennon's time? Well, later than Glennon. Old bass players?

Not personally. I might have seen him, but not to know him. You know what Billy Murray, huh? Billy Murray? No, I heard of him. I never did meet him. Thank you. You can meet him a little more. Old man Mitchell's and Mr. Glennon. I used to see them quite often.
